parts.note: the throne is jocular slang for a toilet, so the throne room is the lav
the suffix -ish means somewhat like, as in greenish

explanation.surface: A lavish lifestyle compared to a monarch's grand throne room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Throne room' suggests a palace, but the throne here is the toilet: LAV is British slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe spending or giving with great generosity and no restraint; they are synonyms.

clue.text: Bar talk from members consuming beer with ecstasy

indicators.note: consuming means the first piece swallows the second inside it

parts.note: legs are limbs, members of the body
ale is a kind of beer
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Pub chat from club members drinking beer and taking pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub, but here it means the legal profession: barristers are 'called to the Bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bar is the body of barristers, and their jargon is the technical language of law.

indicators.note: keeping means the first word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: vile means wicked or evil

indicators.note: rent here is the past tense of rend, torn apart, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A greedy landlord keeps changing rents and rates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' reads as money paid to a landlord, but here it is the past tense of rend, torn apart, which signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Something versatile adapts readily to many uses, so it is changeable in the sense of adaptable.

parts.note: kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: Someone hiding from their relatives down south.
explanation.definitionFit: A hide is an animal's pelt, the outer covering of the body; a synonym in the noun sense.

clue.text: Entrusts passwords to guard back in barbican, if recalled

indicators.note: to guard means the outer word protects the letters placed inside it

parts.note: codes are secret words used to gain access, like passwords

indicators.note: back in points to the final letter of the word barbican
recalled means called back, so the word if is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone shares security codes with the guards at a fortified gate.
explanation.walkthrough: A barbican is a fortified gateway, which makes 'guard' read as a sentry; it is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To confide is to tell secrets in trust, so confides is a synonym of entrusts in this sense.

clue.text: What you are regarding feels awkward

parts.note: on means regarding or about, as in a book on birds

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters of feels are jumbled

explanation.surface: Self-conscious musing about how you feel when uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person is their own self, so a playful definition describes the identity that you are.

indicators.note: interfering in means the first piece pushes into the middle of the other

parts.note: forests are examples of ecosystems
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everybody meddling in the natural environment does harm.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall is to prevent or obstruct something beforehand, so it is a synonym of hinders.

clue.text: Peddled drugs with a fallen foreign character

indicators.note: fallen means the letter a drops down to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: dealt is what a dealer did with drugs, peddled them

explanation.surface: A drug dealer falls from grace.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'fallen' moves the A in DEALT to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Delta is the fourth letter of the Greek alphabet, hence a foreign character.

definitions.meaning: to caress or pass a hand softly over something
butterfly is one style of swimming, along with crawl and backstroke

explanation.surface: Softly touching a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a soft caress with the hand, and also a style of swimming, butterfly being one example.

indicators.note: welcoming means the first word takes the second in

parts.note: to give is to yield or sag under weight
vin is the French word for wine

explanation.surface: Offering a discount on French wine to welcome customers.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving is an amount taken off a price, the same as a discount; a noun synonym.

clue.text: Start to develop golf — stop losing lead

parts.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: losing lead means the word drops its first letter

parts.note: to terminate is to stop or end

explanation.surface: A golfer's game develops, then stalls after losing the lead in a tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds germinate when they begin to grow, so the word means to start developing.

indicators.note: introducing means the first piece leads in the one after it

parts.note: to rule is to judge or decide officially

explanation.surface: A judge brings in the correct measure.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler is a straight strip used for measuring lengths, a measure in the sense of a gauge.

indicators.note: to feed means the letter is put into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a lad is a youth or young man
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: No cost to feed a young person.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is what a gun or vehicle carries; load is a synonym in the sense of a burden or charge put in.

clue.text: Rogue rigs the ship for marine hunter

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward or out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ark is Noah's ship

explanation.surface: A rogue sailor rigging a ship to go hunting at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' rearranges RIGS THE to TIGERSH, and then ARK is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This striped shark is a large predatory fish of warm seas, hunting at sea.

clue.text: Bill people after fair time for alteration

indicators.note: after places the word for people following the word for fair

parts.note: an ad is a bill, a printed advertisement or poster
just means fair
men are people

explanation.surface: Bill and others arrive after the fair for a change of plan.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjustment is a small change made to something, so it is a synonym of alteration.

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: ignoring means the letters for people are left out of indignation

parts.note: a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Keep quiet about your indignation and ignore everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is British slang for a party, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is a lively party, and a do is the informal British word for a social event.

clue.text: Learner involved in great times hanging loose

indicators.note: involved in means the letter goes inside the following word

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means great
L is a learner, from the L-plate on learner cars
by means times in multiplication, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A learner having great times while hanging loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby flesh is slack and soft, sagging or hanging loose rather than firm.

clue.text: Good to acquire, operable refurbished propeller

indicators.note: refurbished means done up anew, so the letters are put in fresh order

explanation.surface: A good second-hand propeller, now working again after refurbishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to acquire' says OPERABLE takes in the G before 'refurbished' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pole is pushed against the riverbed to propel a canal boat, so it is a propeller.

clue.text: Outline in hills is pony stable to the north

indicators.note: to the north says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sketch of hill country where a pony is stabled in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to the north' means read upwards: the letters hidden in 'hilLS IS PONY Stable' are written in from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A synopsis is a brief summary or outline of a story or argument.

indicators.note: concealed by means the record is hidden inside the following word

parts.note: a duty is a tax on goods
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A tax official hiding the books.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is a person appointed to act for another, an official below the top post.

indicators.note: opening in points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: an awning is a canopy of fabric over a deck or window

explanation.surface: A gap opening up in the canopy over a yacht.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning hole is wide open, so it is a synonym of gaping.

clue.text: Foolishness of mine trapping a bird

indicators.note: trapping means the first word encloses what follows

parts.note: my and mine both mean belonging to me
the lark is a songbird

explanation.surface: My silly antics catching a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Malarkey, also spelt without the E, is informal for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Physician from foreign land, exchanging Germany for centre of Wrexham

indicators.note: exchanging says one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: Mexico is a foreign country

indicators.note: centre of points to the middle letter of Wrexham

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A doctor from abroad trades a German post for one in Wrexham, a town in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Wrexham has seven letters, so its centre is the fourth, X, which D replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Medico is an informal word for a doctor or medical student, a synonym of physician.

clue.text: Coppers upset receiving lip in stint

indicators.note: receiving means the outer letters take in the other word
upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: PCs are police constables, coppers
a rim is the lip of a cup

explanation.surface: Upset policemen getting lip during their shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stint' looks like a noun for a spell of duty, but it is the verb: to be sparing.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to be thrifty and economise, the same as to stint on something.

clue.text: Change now due with city and across region

indicators.note: change tells the solver to alter the order of the letters

explanation.surface: A change in a city spreads across the region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change' rearranges NOW DUE and CITY together.
explanation.definitionFit: Countywide means extending throughout a county, an administrative region of Britain.

indicators.note: supporting in a down entry means the second word sits below the first

parts.note: a sage is a wise master or teacher

explanation.surface: A master holding up university tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is customary practice, and a convention is an accepted way of doing things.

indicators.note: disheartened means the word noble loses its heart, leaving its outer letters
retreating means the letters for soldiers go backwards

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A Roman aristocrat dismayed as his soldiers fall back.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor, so the definition names him by nationality as one example.

indicators.note: when climbing means the word goes upwards in this down entry, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Going at the wrong speed when climbing a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A trot is a gait, a moderate running pace of a horse or person.

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a journal

explanation.surface: An international European magazine and its public face.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something, so it is a synonym of representation.

parts.note: to incur is to acquire or bring upon oneself, a gain in a loose sense
IOUs are notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: Someone told they can gain debts shrugs indifferently.
explanation.definitionFit: Being incurious means lacking curiosity, so not interested in things around you.

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quietly
the rest are the others

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word mingled

explanation.surface: Standing quietly while the other guests mingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Prestige is high status in the eyes of others, a person's standing or reputation.

clue.text: Pressure second player to drop account

indicators.note: to drop means the letters for account are removed

parts.note: an actress is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A supporting actor is pressured into dropping their story.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress is mental or physical strain, a synonym of pressure.
